1.name: Madrazo's Golden Idol
1.flavor: The golden face of the Caida Libre legend — a Madrazo family good-luck charm.

2.name: Impotent Rage Figure
2.flavor: Original collector edition of the Vinewood Superhero — pedestal still gleaming.

3.name: Alien Figure
3.flavor: A rare casting hunted by secret collectors.

5.name: Beast Figure
5.flavor: Half-monster antagonist from the Vinewood Superhero series — furry edition.

6.name: Sasquatch Figure
6.flavor: Holy grail of "Bigfoot" Easter egg hunters.

7.name: Rockstar Classic Logo
7.flavor: Limited-run studio memorabilia — fallen out of a display case.

8.name: Rockstar Community Award
8.flavor: Plaque pressed for Rockstar community members — only one of its kind in Pillbox Hill.

12.name: Pop Art Sculpture #1
12.flavor: Retro pop-art piece from the Diamond Casino Heritage Hall.

13.name: Pop Art Sculpture #2
13.flavor: Same artist's second run — fewer pressed.

15.name: Panther Statue
15.flavor: Dark bronze panther — its eyes still follow you.

16.name: Horse Statue
16.flavor: Vintage horse sculpture — lost by a collector years ago.

17.name: Abstract Sculpture
17.flavor: Meaning unclear, price steep — they call it real art.

19.name: Vintage Hero Figure
19.flavor: 80s Vinewood kids' collectible — straight out of the original box.

21.name: Plush Dog
21.flavor: A lost holiday gift — never reached its owner.

22.name: Sunny — Summer Festival Mascot
22.flavor: Signature mascot of the Vespucci summer festival — eyes still Pacific blue.

23.name: Bruno the Vinewood Bear
23.flavor: Pixel Pete claw-machine signature prize — "Bruno" tag stitched on its fur.

24.name: Po the Davis Panda
24.flavor: Davis neighborhood claw-machine legend — still sweet-eyed.

25.name: Kobi the Cute Koala
25.flavor: Top-shelf plush with an "I'm cute" tag on its ear.

26.name: Lily the Bunny
26.flavor: A love memento — left at a club entrance, red ribbon on its ear.

27.name: Foxxy the Little Fox
27.flavor: Burger Shot game-corner mascot — patched tail.

28.name: Zara the Giraffe
28.flavor: Miracle morale-booster of the Pillbox Hospital waiting room — tall neck and all.

29.name: Toto the Tiger
29.flavor: Silent witness of the Vanilla Unicorn stage — VIP badge on its neck.

30.name: Lucky the Dog
30.flavor: Pixel Pete's final-season prize — a lucky charm for those who complete the collection.

31.name: Vinewood Garden Gnome
31.flavor: A surviving member of the Vinewood Hills gnome cult — Rockstar's oldest backyard prank.

32.name: Rearing Horse Figurine
32.flavor: A cast-bronze racehorse trinket — the kind of thing a Vinewood agent keeps to look classier than he is.

33.name: Modern Sculpture #4
33.flavor: Penthouse-rotation modern piece — Tao Cheng signed the certificate himself.

34.name: Cartel Office Sculpture
34.flavor: Sat on the cartel foreman's desk at the Cluckin' Bell processing plant — slightly chicken-grease stained.

35.name: Flipper Champion Trophy
35.flavor: Top-grade Arena War silverware — won by the only driver who finished Flipper on his wheels.

36.name: Ron's Lucky Cap
36.flavor: Ron Jakowski wore this through every Sandy Shores conspiracy stream — radiation reading: borderline.

37.name: Jeroboam of Blêuter'd
37.flavor: A 3-litre Jeroboam of Blêuter'd '08 — left behind in the VIP booth, untouched.

38.name: Vintage Gamepad
38.flavor: The controller from Jimmy De Santa's all-nighter — sticky thumbsticks included.

39.name: Pop Art Car #10
39.flavor: Diamond Heritage Gallery — pop-art tribute to the muscle cars of Los Santos' golden decade.

40.name: Pop Art Car #12
40.flavor: The second half of the Diamond muscle-car diptych — the one Avi Schwartzman tried to lift.

41.name: Pop Art Car #9
41.flavor: Opening piece of the Pop-Art Car triptych — never auctioned, never insured.

42.name: Idol Trophy — Lesser Aztec
42.flavor: Display-case twin of the Casino Heist's prized idol — the cartel kept it as a bragging trophy.

43.name: Idol Trophy — Greater Aztec
43.flavor: A Cluckin' Bell back-office trophy — cartel boss's homage to the Casino Heist that started it all.

44.name: Sun-Stone Planet Trophy
44.flavor: The planetary piece of the Aztec board-set — one of four trophies Cluckin' Bell's boss kept on the office shelf.

45.name: Scarab Tank Trophy
45.flavor: Bronze Scarab tank cast for the Arena War champion who survived the demolition derby finals — base still smells like burnt rubber.

46.name: Aztec Treasure Hoard
46.flavor: A cluster of Aztec coins and chain links — cartel "tax" skimmed off the original Casino Heist.

47.name: Raw Aztec Idol
47.flavor: Loose from its display case — pulled mid-heist, never re-mounted.

48.name: Twin Aztec Idol
48.flavor: Younger twin of the Madrazo idol — same mould, different smelter.

49.name: Aztec Sun-Egg Trophy
49.flavor: The Aztec sun-egg — completes the four-piece trophy shelf alongside idol, scarab, and planet.

50.name: Golden Pogo Trophy
50.flavor: Lucky Wheel grand-prize collectible — they only minted twelve, allegedly.

51.name: Retro Console Art Piece
51.flavor: Vintage console treated as gallery art — Pixel Pete weeps every time it sells.

52.name: "For the Love of Cash" Diamond Skull
52.flavor: A penthouse vanity piece stolen during the original Casino Heist — its pavé diamonds are real, and Lester still has the appraisal.

53.name: Tataryn Imperial Egg
53.flavor: A Tataryn family heirloom that vanished overnight — the morning after Avi Schwartzman left town.

54.name: El Rubio Reserva Añejo
54.flavor: Smuggled off Cayo Perico in a duffel bag — the seal is intact and the wax stamp is still El Rubio's.

55.name: Declasse Sabre GT Maquette
55.flavor: Commissioned by Tao Cheng's father after a winning night at the high-limit blackjack table.

56.name: "OG1" South Central Plaque
56.flavor: Lifted off a Davis garage wall — old heads say it belonged to Stretch back when Grove Street still meant something.

57.name: LS Panic Game-Ball
57.flavor: Signed in faded Sharpie by the entire Los Santos Panic defensive line after their '08 division win.

58.name: Vespucci Streetball Tournament Ball
58.flavor: Worn down to the rubber on the Vespucci courts — the "Lamar 23" marker is still legible.

59.name: Pogo The Monkey Plush
59.flavor: Claw-machine grand prize from the Up-n-Atom diner's back-room arcade — tag says "Property of Tracey."

60.name: El Rubio's Marksman Trophy
60.flavor: Awarded by El Rubio himself to his top compound sniper — engraved "Para mi mejor tirador, 2020."

61.name: Gilded Bowling Pin (Lebowski Edition)
61.flavor: An unironic six-figure homage to the great American pastime — Tao Cheng has three.

62.name: Macbeth 30yr Crystal Decanter
62.flavor: Lifted from a Maze Bank executive's private bar — the engraved monogram reads "AB," same initials as Avon Hertz's accountant.

63.name: Festive Surprise Triple-Score Trophy
63.flavor: Awarded to Arena contestants who scored a hat-trick during the Festive Surprise event — the bows are still curled.

64.name: Master Bandito Pilot Trophy
64.flavor: Earned for ten kinetic-mine kills in the RC Bandito — Arena fans still call this the "garage-floor trophy."

65.name: Arena Career Ascendant Tower
65.flavor: Awarded for surviving 100 consecutive Arena rounds — Benny himself welded the base plate.

66.name: Arena Grand Champion Cup
66.flavor: The grand prize Mr. Bossman handed out at the inaugural Arena finals — only three were ever cast, and two are missing.

67.name: Pegassi Toreador Chrome Maquette
67.flavor: A scale piece commissioned to mark the Toreador's debut on Vinewood Boulevard.

68.name: LS Caesars Slugger Bobblehead
68.flavor: A '90s souvenir from the old LS Caesars dugout — Franklin keeps one on his desk for luck.

69.name: San Andreas Stallions Rookie Bobblehead
69.flavor: Vinewood Bowl giveaway from the '04 home opener — the spring head still wobbles after twenty years.

70.name: Arena Workshop Pit-Boss Mug
70.flavor: "World's #1 Boss" mug from Mr. Bossman himself — coffee ring still on the rim.

71.name: Benefactor Krieger Display Maquette
71.flavor: A million-chip showpiece from the Penthouse gallery — Yung Ancestor name-dropped this exact sculpture in a verse.

72.name: Gilded "Free Throw" Sculpture
72.flavor: A six-figure conversation piece — the artist's signature, "Jeff K.," is etched on the underside.

73.name: Porcelain Girl Figurine
73.flavor: A chipped little porcelain girl that once lived on a Vinewood mantelpiece — pretty, naive, and worth more than she looks.

74.name: Harlequin Clown Figurine
74.flavor: A pierrot doll with cracked enamel and a smile that always looks one frame off.

75.name: Cypress Abstract Sculpture
75.flavor: Hipster gallery piece left on a Cypress Flats loading dock — labeled "untitled #4" and priced like it matters.

76.name: Bronze Stallion Figurine
76.flavor: A miniature stallion that used to live on Michael De Santa's mantelpiece — somebody snatched it during the Madrazo fallout.

77.name: Inkwell Skull Trophy
77.flavor: A flash-art skull lifted straight off the counter of a Harmony tattoo parlor — still smells like green soap.

78.name: OG Mixtape — Variant 2
78.flavor: Sealed promo tape from a bootlegged West Coast pressing — Franklin would pay double for this.

79.name: Chrome Gladiator Skull
79.flavor: Hood-ornament-sized skull plated in show-chrome — an Arena War champion's nightstand piece.

80.name: Lowrider Art Maquette
80.flavor: A gallery maquette of a chopped lowrider — pinstripes still wet to the touch.

81.name: El Rubio's Racer Trophy
81.flavor: A gilded racer trophy lifted from a private island vault — the engraving has been scratched off.

82.name: Downtown Cab Co. Gold Trophy
82.flavor: A century-of-service award from the Downtown Cab Co. — last seen on a dispatcher's shelf before the place got robbed.

83.name: Crystal Pyramid Paperweight
83.flavor: A heavy crystal pyramid that used to weigh down a producer's contracts — supposedly clears bad energy.

84.name: Champion's Boxing Glove
84.flavor: A single red glove left in a corner of a long-closed gym — knuckle dust still on the leather.

85.name: Galaxy Yacht Miniature
85.flavor: A jeweler's scale model of the Galaxy — gold plating, working anchor, priced like the real thing.

86.name: Up-n-Atomizer Raygun
86.flavor: A retro chrome death-ray straight out of the Up-n-Atom diner sign — and surprisingly heavy when you pick it up.

87.name: Brutalist Concrete Block
87.flavor: A poured-concrete art block that the gallery insists is "post-Vinewood brutalist" — even though it looks like a curb.

88.name: Maze Bank Tower Maquette
88.flavor: A perfect scale model of Maze Bank Tower — the dollhouse a CEO keeps in the corner of his real office.

89.name: Perico Compliance Stungun
89.flavor: A black-market stungun pulled off an island guard — still has a half-charge in the cell.

90.name: Aztec Stone Idol
90.flavor: A volcanic-stone idol older than the city itself — Franklin swore he never bought it, but it kept showing up.

91.name: Arena Wars Champion Trophy
91.flavor: The big one — solid-gold sole-survivor trophy, awarded once per Arena Wars season and never twice.

92.name: Pink-Frosted Sprinkle Donut
92.flavor: A half-eaten pink-frosted ring with rainbow sprinkles, left on a napkin during a long stakeout.

93.name: Crystal Champagne Flute
93.flavor: Lipstick still on the rim from a Vinewood afterparty nobody remembers leaving.

94.name: Cayo Perico Dancer Trophy
94.flavor: A gilded dancer figurine, won in a heist crew bet and stashed for a rainy day.

95.name: Cayo Perico Battler Trophy
95.flavor: Twin to the dancer, this one was claimed by the muscle of the crew before they vanished.

96.name: Penthouse Decorative Sculpture
96.flavor: Modernist art piece pawned by a broke arcade owner; the rich never knew it was missing.

97.name: Meteorite Chocolate Bar
97.flavor: Bingo-themed candy bar with a wrapper claiming it was forged in deep space.

98.name: P's & Q's Candy Box
98.flavor: A sticky carton of alphabet candy left behind after a kid's birthday went sideways.

99.name: Wall-Mounted Concert Speaker
99.flavor: A scuffed PA speaker liberated from a Vespucci block party that the LSPD shut down at 2 a.m.

100.name: Bean Machine Takeaway Coffee
100.flavor: Lukewarm latte with the lid loose — abandoned on the way to a meeting that already started.

101.name: Tagger's Paint Brush
101.flavor: Bristles caked in fluorescent green — dropped mid-tag when sirens hit the alley.

102.name: Numbered Pool Ball — 8
102.flavor: The black ball, scuffed from a thousand grudge matches over five-dollar bets.

103.name: Numbered Pool Ball — 7
103.flavor: Maroon stripe rolled off the table and never made it back to the rack.

104.name: Numbered Pool Ball — 9
104.flavor: Yellow stripe, scratched along one side where someone palmed it as a paperweight.

105.name: Numbered Pool Ball — 13
105.flavor: Orange stripe with a chipped lacquer corner from a hard bank shot gone wrong.

106.name: Numbered Pool Ball — 11
106.flavor: Burgundy stripe stained with cigarette ash — once a regular at a Del Perro tournament.

107.name: Numbered Pool Ball — 5
107.flavor: Solid orange, smooth as new — clearly stolen on its first night out of the box.

108.name: Numbered Pool Ball — 15
108.flavor: Maroon stripe with a hairline crack that whistles when struck just right.

109.name: Numbered Pool Ball — 12
109.flavor: Purple stripe found in the pocket of a borrowed jacket no one returned.

110.name: Numbered Pool Ball — 4
110.flavor: Solid violet, polished to a near mirror — the favorite of a long-retired hustler.

111.name: White Cue Ball
111.flavor: The cue ball that broke a thousand racks — chalk smudge still on its leading edge.

112.name: Numbered Pool Ball — 6
112.flavor: Solid green with a dent from when it doubled as a paperweight in a debt collector's office.

113.name: Numbered Pool Ball — 1
113.flavor: Solid yellow, the lucky one — palmed before every break by a regular at the bar.

114.name: Numbered Pool Ball — 2
114.flavor: Solid blue with a faded marker initial — claimed long ago, never reclaimed.

115.name: Numbered Pool Ball — 3
115.flavor: Solid red — said to be from a table where a famous one-pocket hustle went down.

116.name: Numbered Pool Ball — 10
116.flavor: Blue stripe with the felt scuff from one of the tables nobody is allowed to fix.

117.name: Numbered Pool Ball — 14
117.flavor: Green stripe missing from a Cypress Flats garage table; nobody asked twice.

118.name: Glazed Ceramic Jug
118.flavor: A heavy ceramic jug from a Grand Senora roadside stand — chipped lip, still holds water.

119.name: Rolled Architectural Paper
119.flavor: Building blueprints rolled tight and tied with twine — dropped during a hasty exit.

120.name: Customized SMG Mk II
120.flavor: A modded SMG with a serial filed clean — left behind after a Paleto Bay job went loud.

121.name: Industrial Claw Hammer
121.flavor: A heavy claw hammer borrowed from a foreman and never returned to the toolbelt.

122.name: Barber's Lather Cup
122.flavor: Half-used barber's foam, sandalwood scent baked in.

123.name: Pneumatic Impact Driver
123.flavor: Trigger sticky with brake dust and old grease.

124.name: Channel Surfer Remote
124.flavor: Battery cover taped on with a square of duct.

125.name: Wicker Laundry Hamper
125.flavor: Smells like fabric softener and a missing sock.

126.name: Locked Burner Slab
126.flavor: Locked screen lit with twenty-two missed calls.

127.name: Chrome Cocktail Shaker
127.flavor: Still cold, ice rattling against polished steel.

128.name: Two-Finger Whisky Pour
128.flavor: Smoky, peaty, two fingers of regret.

129.name: Marble Curio Sculpt
129.flavor: Cold to the touch, signed on the base in pencil.

130.name: Stack of Forged Licenses
130.flavor: Twelve identities, same haircut, different names.

131.name: White-Gold Sapphire Drop
131.flavor: Set in white gold, weight uneven on purpose.

132.name: Drum-Mag Street Sweeper
132.flavor: Drum mag warm, serial number etched off.

133.name: Crusted Kibble Bowl
133.flavor: Crusted with dried gravy, ants taking a meeting.

134.name: Spent Brass Cartridge
134.flavor: Primer struck dead center, lacquer flaked off the case.

135.name: Dust-Wrapped Hardback
135.flavor: Spine cracked at chapter four, dog-eared and final.

136.name: Wired Computer Mouse
136.flavor: Scroll wheel sticky, left button worn shiny.

137.name: Bedside Alarm Clock
137.flavor: Display stuck at 12:00, snooze button caved in.

138.name: Folded Dossier
138.flavor: Names redacted in marker, edges curled by humidity.

139.name: Two-Slice Toaster
139.flavor: Crumbs in the tray, lever sprung loose.

140.name: Bruised Red Apple
140.flavor: One bite taken, set down and forgotten.

141.name: Slim DVD Deck
141.flavor: Disc tray jammed, RCA cables tangled in a knot.

142.name: Brick of C4
142.flavor: Detonator unscrewed, putty soft and warm.

143.name: Pride Lager Can
143.flavor: Sweating cold, half a thumbprint on the tab.

144.name: Paparazzi Camera Body
144.flavor: Long lens scuffed, last frame still in the buffer.

145.name: Cut-Glass Executive Ashtray
145.flavor: Heavy bottom, three cigars logged in tonight.

146.name: Mounted Taxi Meter
146.flavor: Frozen at $14.20, cable dangling from the dash bracket.

147.name: Princess-Cut Diamond Solitaire
147.flavor: Princess cut, certified to a name that no longer exists.

148.name: Air Hockey Mallet
148.flavor: Felt bottom worn smooth, handle sweat-stained.

149.name: Black Obelisk Figurine
149.flavor: Polished stone, base etched with a single symbol.

150.name: Dented eCola Can
150.flavor: Dented at the rim, condensation pooling at the base.

151.name: Casino Glossy Quarterly
151.flavor: Crisp glossy pages bragging about jackpots that nobody you know has ever won.

152.name: Clubhouse Burner Laptop
152.flavor: Sticker-plastered laptop with a battery hot enough to fry an egg on.

153.name: Grease-Crusted Tool Caddy
153.flavor: Every drawer rattles with mismatched sockets and a single greasy fortune cookie.

154.name: Imported Cigar Stash
154.flavor: Wrapped tight in foil and smelling like a richer man's living room.

155.name: Crystal Whisky Decanter
155.flavor: Hand-cut crystal that still holds the ghost of a thirty-year-old single malt.

156.name: Bottle-Service Ice Bucket
156.flavor: Half-melted ice, lipstick rim, and an aftertaste of someone else's good night.

157.name: Unlabeled DVD Case
157.flavor: No title, no rating, and a sticky residue you do not want to identify.

158.name: Heavy Steel Wrench
158.flavor: The kind of wrench that has tightened more jaws than bolts.

159.name: One Lonely Boot
159.flavor: Sole worn through, story untold, second boot probably in a dumpster somewhere.

160.name: Drained House Bottle
160.flavor: Sticky label peeled, contents long gone, a tiny stage for fruit flies.

161.name: Penthouse Brass Sculpt
161.flavor: Cast brass with a curve so smug it must have cost a quarter million.

162.name: Cut Sapphire Pendant
162.flavor: Cold to the touch and somehow heavier than a stone that small should be.

163.name: Garden Center Fern
163.flavor: Slightly overwatered, slightly underloved, ready to die in a new home.

164.name: Taped-Grip Snubnose Revolver
164.flavor: Six chambers, two spent, grip wrapped in friction tape that smells like sweat.

165.name: Scuffed Speaker Dock
165.flavor: Battery dead, bass blown, but the antenna still glows a hopeful blue.

166.name: Half-Empty Spray Can
166.flavor: Rattles when you shake it, hisses when you press it, sings when you aim it.

167.name: Crumpled Soda Cup
167.flavor: Straw bent, lid bitten, just enough syrup left to glue it to the curb.

168.name: Surplus Gas Mask
168.flavor: Filter cartridge crusted, eye lenses fogged with someone else's panic.

169.name: Executive Smartphone
169.flavor: Locked screen, two missed calls, lockscreen photo of a yacht you cannot afford.

170.name: Warm Shell Casing
170.flavor: Brass still warm enough to remember the trigger pull.

171.name: Popped Magnum Champagne
171.flavor: Foil torn, cork lost, the night already on its way to being legendary.

172.name: Iron Battle Axe
172.flavor: Edge nicked, haft worn smooth, the kind of thing that belongs over a fireplace.

173.name: Sealed Smuggler Whisky
173.flavor: Amber inside, untouched, label embossed with a name nobody pronounces right.

174.name: Pearl-Grip Vintage Pistol
174.flavor: Engraved barrel, mother-of-pearl grip, smells faintly of gun oil and regret.

175.name: Half-Full Wine Glass
175.flavor: Lipstick on the rim, sediment at the bottom, conversation long abandoned.

176.name: Heavy .50 Handgun
176.flavor: Recoil bruise material, with a serial number filed clean down to silver.

177.name: Tall Glass Waterpipe
177.flavor: Cloudy chamber, cracked downstem, scented like a Vinewood music video set.

178.name: Squeezed Mustard Bottle
178.flavor: Crusted nozzle, dented sides, lid missing in action.

179.name: Crushed Soda Can
179.flavor: Tab still attached, side caved in by a boot that was in a hurry.

180.name: Stenciled Ammo Crate
180.flavor: Stamped with a unit number, sealed with packing tape and a prayer.

181.name: Cracked DVD Case
181.flavor: A scuffed plastic case with the disc missing and a faded rental sticker.

182.name: Emergency Flare Box
182.flavor: A scorched cardboard box stenciled with red hazard warnings.

183.name: Gilded Skull Bust II
183.flavor: A chromed memento-mori someone walked off with before the unveiling.

184.name: Kitchen Glass Pot
184.flavor: A heat-stained Pyrex pot still smelling faintly of marinara.

185.name: Front-Office Briefcase
185.flavor: A scratched aluminum case latched with a luggage tag in Italian.

186.name: Cubicle Desk Tidy
186.flavor: A loaded pen cup that has clearly never been organized.

187.name: Aztec Idol Cache
187.flavor: A pre-Columbian curio crusted in jungle moss; someone really shouldn't have moved it.

188.name: Sidewalk Litter Pile
188.flavor: Crushed cups, a lotto ticket, and a flyer for a club that closed in 2014.

189.name: MC Courier Case
189.flavor: A locked road case stickered over by three different chapters.

190.name: Resident DJ Laptop
190.flavor: Battle-scarred deck still cued to a track nobody admits writing.

191.name: Boutique Display Vase
191.flavor: A hand-thrown ceramic with a price tag worth a month of rent.

192.name: Dropped 9mm Sidearm
192.flavor: Slide locked back, serials filed clean, three rounds shy of a magazine.

193.name: Gilded Skull Bust III
193.flavor: A matching piece from the unfinished casino installation triptych.

194.name: LSPD Maglite
194.flavor: Heavy aluminum, a dented bezel, and a body cam clip still attached.

195.name: Mom-and-Pop CLOSED Sign
195.flavor: Hand-flipped a thousand times; corners curled, hours scratched out twice.

196.name: Stray Designer Trainer
196.flavor: Right foot only, scuffed toe, laces still tied — somebody ran.

197.name: Lowland Peyote Bloom
197.flavor: A waxy desert button that hums faintly when you crouch beside it.

198.name: Industrial Oil Drum
198.flavor: Bulging seams and a fresh leak slicking the gravel underneath.

199.name: Surplus Ammo Box
199.flavor: Military-stamped, half-open, count clearly off the books.

200.name: Executive Rolodex
200.flavor: A flipper full of penciled names; every third entry is crossed out.

201.name: Casino Art Car Sculpture
201.flavor: A chromed muscle-car silhouette mounted like a hood ornament gone feral.

202.name: Vintage Transistor Radio
202.flavor: Cracked tuner dial, still picks up Los Santos Rock if you tap it right.

203.name: Gilded Skull Bust I
203.flavor: The first of the triptych — the one the artist refused to title.

204.name: Smuggled Whisky Bottle
204.flavor: Foreign label, broken seal, the import stamp clumsily scratched off.

205.name: Discarded Novelty Toy
205.flavor: Found behind the dumpster; nobody is admitting whose it was.

206.name: Headshop Centerpiece
206.flavor: Hand-blown borosilicate, smoked-over chamber, sticker price already debated.

207.name: Chrome Salon Hairdryer
207.flavor: Heavy chrome handle, motor still warm to the touch.

208.name: Cream of Tomato Can
208.flavor: Dented label, expiration scrubbed off with a marker.

209.name: Workshop Tool Chest
209.flavor: Top drawer hanging open; sockets in metric, ratchets in imperial.

210.name: Casino Court Trophy Ball
210.flavor: A gilded basketball sculpture, signed in marker by a name half-smudged.

211.name: Stenciled Ammo Crate II
211.flavor: Brass casings rattle inside like loose teeth in a coffee can.

212.name: Velvet Heirloom Box
212.flavor: Tiny brass hinges still smell of someone's grandmother.

213.name: Gilt Hood Maquette
213.flavor: Lacquer thick enough to mortgage a small studio apartment.

214.name: Executive Bust Sculpt
214.flavor: Some VP picked it; the assistant rolled her eyes.

215.name: Skipping CD Stack
215.flavor: Half the cases are empty; the rest are scratched to hell.

216.name: Counter Ammo Box
216.flavor: Sticker says SALE; the box has never moved.

217.name: Bar Citrus Jar
217.flavor: A lone wedge floats like it's waiting for a tip.

218.name: Knockoff Bomb Device
218.flavor: Wires the color of cheap candy and a timer that doesn't tick.

219.name: Window Display Toy
219.flavor: Even the alley cats walk wide around this one.

220.name: Resin Tower Bong
220.flavor: The water hasn't been changed since the previous tenant.

221.name: Cut Crystal Cigar Tray
221.flavor: Three cigar ends, all Cubans, all stubbed mid-deal.

222.name: Counter Toaster
222.flavor: The dial is stuck on five and nobody's complained yet.

223.name: Bloodied Garden Spade
223.flavor: Dirt on the blade looks redder than topsoil should.

224.name: Anonymous Brown Parcel
224.flavor: No return address, three different postage stickers.

225.name: No.1 Arcade Trophy
225.flavor: Engraving reads NUMBER ONE in a font from 1983.

226.name: Pharmacy Aisle Bottle
226.flavor: Off-brand label, store-brand smell, full-price tag.

227.name: Cut Mixing Tube
227.flavor: Residue rings around the inside like a bad year for trees.

228.name: Tactical Plate Mask
228.flavor: Strap still smells like the last guy's adrenaline.

229.name: Black Untitled Sculpt
229.flavor: Catalog calls it Untitled; the accountant calls it a write-off.

230.name: Sealed Champion Bottle
230.flavor: Plaque date is older than most of the arcade's regulars.

231.name: Hard-Foam Gun Case
231.flavor: Foam inset still shaped for something serious.

232.name: Cayo Salt-Rim Jar
